nina: hey all, day 1 question. I imported the kubeconfig from Okta and tried `kubectl get pods -n realtime-systems` and got Forbidden. who owns that namespace?
nina: exact error: `Error from server (Forbidden): pods is forbidden: User "nina@redwood.com" cannot list resource "pods" in API group "" in the namespace "realtime-systems"`
devops: welcome! quick checks: `kubectl config current-context` and `kubectl auth can-i list pods --namespace=realtime-systems`. also `kubectl config view --minify` to confirm which user is active. paste outputs (no kubeconfigs).
nina: `kubectl config current-context` -> `staging-nina`
nina: `kubectl auth can-i list pods --namespace=realtime-systems` -> `no`
team-platform: realtime-systems is owned by eng-realtime. we gate via SSO group `eng-realtime-devs`. new hires sometimes miss the group sync. do you have SSO id and github handle?
nina: SSO id nina@redwood.com, github ninaq
team-platform: i can add a namespace-scoped RoleBinding with `view` for a few hours so you can finish onboarding. would you prefer 4h or 12h?
nina: 4h should be enough, thanks.
team-platform: running:
```
kubectl create rolebinding onb-nina-realtime -n realtime-systems --clusterrole=view --user=nina@redwood.com --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
```
team-platform: applied. retry the `kubectl get pods -n realtime-systems`
onboard-bot: FYI the onboarding guide has a step for persistent access requests: https://internal.redwood/docs/onboard/kube-access - use the infra access form for long-lived group mapping.
nina: retried and pods show up, thanks :tada: 
nina: quick follow-up: I want to port-forward a pod for local testing (`kubectl port-forward`). do I need extra permissions?
devops: `port-forward` uses the `pods/portforward` subresource; `view` usually covers it but some clusters forbid it. if you get Forbidden for port-forward we can add `create` on `pods/portforward` in a Role.
team-platform: note: we avoid granting cluster-wide permissions; we'll add a Role with the `pods/portforward` verb if needed. open a quick DM if port-forward fails.
nina: got it. last Q: any tips to avoid running things against prod when you have multiple kubeconfigs?
devops: keep separate files and use `KUBECONFIG` when merging intentionally. alias we use: `kc() { kubectl --context="$1" "${@:2}"; }` then `kc staging get pods -n realtime-systems`. also set the namespace on the context so plain `kubectl get pods` defaults to the right ns.
nina: perfect, adding to my checklist. thanks everyone!
